# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtorj5fs006b0un, acceptance, add, alias, apache (+136 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, add, approach, art, asserts (+107 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, add, alias, apache, approach (+104 more)

# Intake Brief: Serial Seller: achievement manifest entry + Steamworks API name

## Problem Statement

The new **Serial Seller** challenge (`ch-serial-seller`) must map to a persistent Steam achievement like the existing 12 challenges. The challenge-side mapping is added in the parent item (MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J); this item covers the cross-repo pieces required before the parent can be reviewed.

## Users

- **Producers**: Need the Steam achievement registered on the Steamworks partner backend.
- **Developers**: Need the manifest entry to exist before the drift guard test will pass.
- **Players**: Need the Serial Seller achievement to appear in-game alongside the existing 12 achievements.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` contains a `serial-seller` entry with `steamApiName: TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` and `hidden: false`.
2. The Steamworks partner backend declares the matching `TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` achievement API name.
3. The `core` submodule pointer in the main-street repo is bumped to the commit containing the manifest change.
4. The manifest drift guard (`tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts`) passes with the parent's mapping in place.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The manifest lives in the `core` git submodule (a separate repository: `TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine`), requiring two repo operations.
- The `steamApiName` values must match exactly what is configured on the Steamworks partner backend, or Steam will silently drop the unlock.
- The achievement must not be hidden (`hidden: false`), consistent with the existing 12 challenges.
- The Steamworks backend configuration is a producer/external action that must be completed independently of code changes.

## Existing State

- 12 existing achievements in `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json`, all with the pattern `TCE_MAIN_STREET_<UPPER_SNAKE_CASE>`.
- The manifest is validated by `validateAchievementManifest()` and the drift guard test.
- Precedent: MS-0MUMAZTAY00515MC (bumping core submodule pointer).

## Desired Change

- Add one entry to the manifest for the Serial Seller achievement.
- Commit to the core repo and bump the submodule pointer in main-street.
- Coordinate with the producer to register the achievement on Steamworks.

## Key Files (Predicted)

- `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` — Add `serial-seller` entry
- `core/` (git submodule) — Commit the manifest change
- `.gitmodules` / submodule index — Bump the submodule pointer

## Related Work

- **MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J**: Sell 3 businesses challenge (parent, blocked by this item)
- **MS-0MUNO0M2I004TK04**: Wire Main Street challenges to Steam achievements (parent epic)
- **MS-0MUMAZTAY00515MC**: Precedent for bumping core submodule pointer

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Steamworks backend delay**: If the producer has not yet registered the achievement on Steamworks, the achievement will not unlock for players even after code changes land. This is tracked as a separate action.
- **Scope creep**: Additional achievement metadata (e.g., icons, descriptions) may be desired later; record as a follow-up, not in scope for this item.
- **Submodule conflict**: Unlikely but possible if the core repo has concurrent changes; resolve by rebasing on latest core before bumping.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- This item was already sufficiently defined; no interview questions were asked. The description, scope, and acceptance criteria were clear and actionable.

## Dependency & audit resolution (2026-10-01)

Producer confirmed the Steamworks backend registration (AC2) is not yet done and requires a dependency chain. Two dependency items were created in the core project (CG store — the correct home for Steamworks backend work; worklog does not support cross-store dependency edges, so they are recorded here as cross-project references):

- **CG-0MUPMJVS90019KSQ** — Create the Steamworks project for Tableau Card Engine
- **CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1** — Register Main Street achievements on the Steamworks backend *(depends on CG-0MUPMJVS90019KSQ)*

**AC2 therefore remains unmet until CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1 completes.** This item carries the `do-not-delegate` tag while externally blocked so the downtime worker does not re-dispatch it.

**Merge state:** the item's work is integrated into `dev`/`origin/dev` as commit `dd11ea4` (core → `d2d1f322`). The stale feature branch (which referenced the superseded core commit `4a287d4`) was reset to `dd11ea4`.

**AC4 call:** the drift guard requires the parent challenge-side mapping from **MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J** (which depends on this item, so no cycle is possible). AC4 is verified at parent integration time; the mapping is present uncommitted in the working tree today and will pass permanently once the parent lands.

# Intake Brief: Static docs site for local browsing (VitePress)

**Priority: Low** | **Type: Chore** | **Assignee: Map**

> Discovered from MS-0MUNB54KU005084C as the deferred option (B). Producer
> answers 2026-10-17: still wanted (Q1=A); **navigation-first** use case
> (Q2=A); **local dev tool only**, no CI publishing (Q3=B).

## Headline

Add a VitePress static docs site over the existing `docs/game/` and
`docs/dev/` trees so developers and content authors can browse the docs with
sidebar navigation and rendered Mermaid locally (`npm run docs`); no CI
publishing is required.

## Problem statement

The repo ships docs as a flat, two-tree Markdown forest (`docs/game/`,
`docs/dev/`). Without a site, readers must navigate raw files and there is no
sidebar nav, no search, and no unified landing page. Mermaid fences in docs
(`core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `the-build-gdd.md`) render only with a
Mermaid-aware viewer. A static docs site fixes browsing and renders Mermaid at
build time.

## Users

- **Developers** — need to browse game + dev docs with nav/search while
  working on the codebase.
  - *"As a developer, I want a docs site with sidebar navigation, so I can
    find the right doc faster without guessing file paths."*
- **Game designers / content authors** — need the gameplay reference plus the
  storyline graphs readable in place.
  - *"As a content designer, I want Mermaid diagrams rendered in the docs
    page, so the storyline shape is visible without a Mermaid tool."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Docs site generator** — `vitepress` (MIT) is added as a devDependency
   and a `npm run docs` script serves the docs site locally
   (`vitepress dev docs`); the site root is `docs/` and covers both the
   `docs/game/` and `docs/dev/` trees with sidebar navigation. The
   `docs/.vitepress/` build output is git-ignored and the toolchain stays a
   devDependency only (it never enters the game bundle).
   *Metric: `npm run docs` starts a local server; `npm run docs:build`
   (`vitepress build docs`) exits 0 and emits a static site; `git status`
   stays clean after a build.*
2. **Navigation** — a sidebar (`.vitepress/config.ts`) lists the `docs/game/`
   and `docs/dev/` documents with clear audiences; every top-level `.md` in
   both trees is reachable from the nav (no orphaned docs).
   *Metric: a test asserts every `.md` under `docs/game/` + `docs/dev/` is
   covered by the sidebar config.*
3. **Mermaid rendering** — mermaid code fences in docs render to visible
   diagrams in the built site; the existing committed storyline SVGs
   (`docs/game/assets/storyline-graph-*.svg`) remain usable and are linked or
   embedded as today.
   *Metric: `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` and `the-build-gdd.md`
   render with visible diagrams in the built site.*
4. **No link breakage / no migration** — existing files stay in place under
   `docs/game/` and `docs/dev/`; existing relative links between docs keep
   working; the `docs-path-drift` guard test stays green (no
   `docs/main-street/` or `example-games/main-street/` strings in the new
   VitePress config).
   *Metric: full suite passes including `docs-path-drift.test.ts`.*
5. **Testing/validation** — a pure config-scan unit test validates the docs
   build config (nav coverage + no forbidden paths) with no
   Playwright/browser requirement, and the full project test suite passes
   with the new changes.
   *Metric: the nav-coverage test runs in the `unit` project and asserts every
   top-level `.md` under both trees is listed in the sidebar; `npm test` exits
   0.*
6. **All related documentation is updated** — `docs/README.md` (and/or a new
   `docs/index.md`) documents the docs site plus the `npm run docs` /
   `npm run docs:build` commands, and the README reflects the new scripts.
   *Metric: `docs/README.md` or `docs/index.md` mentions `npm run docs`, and
   the project README documents the docs scripts.*
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.
8. **Local-only, no CI** — no GitHub Pages or docs CI workflow/job is added;
   the `docs` scripts are for local use and the existing game Pages deploy
   workflow is unchanged.
   *Metric: no new or modified workflow file references the docs build; the
   existing deploy workflow is untouched.*
9. **Permissive licence** — `vitepress` and every new plugin/dependency are
   permissively licensed (MIT/Apache-2.0/CC0).
   *Metric: each new dependency's licence is checked and recorded in the
   implementation notes.*
10. **Remote-browser access is documented (WSL caveat)** — the docs pages
   state that `npm run docs` binds to `localhost` only, so a browser running
   outside the dev-server network namespace (the WSL case: server in WSL,
   browser on Windows) cannot load `http://localhost:<port>/`, and give the
   workaround: start the server with `npm run docs -- --host` and open the
   network IP address it prints. Documentation only — no behaviour change is
   required (producer audit rejection, 2026-10-23: "no need to fix this, just
   document it").
   *Metric: `docs/README.md` and `docs/index.md` both name the
   `npm run docs -- --host` invocation and the printed network-IP URL.*

## Constraints

- **Local-only, no CI** — no GitHub Pages workflow, no docs CI job

## Existing state (repo research)

- No docs-site generator present: devDeps include `vite`, `vitest`,
   `playwright`, `mermaid`, `sharp`, `tsx`, `vite-node`, but **no
   `vitepress`/`docusaurus`/`mkdocs`** anywhere in the repo or `core/`.
- `docs/` is plain Markdown: `docs/README.md` index, `docs/game/` (11 files +

   text file and will be scanned — it must avoid those strings.

   (`docs/.vitepress/dist`) must be ignored (add `.vitepress` or
   `docs/.vitepress/dist`).

## Desired change

1. Add `vitepress` (devDependency) and a `docs` npm script.
2. Add `docs/.vitepress/config.ts` with sidebar nav for both trees

3. Theme/plugin for Mermaid rendering (e.g. via the `vitepress-plugin-mermaid`

## Key Files

**Key Files:**

- `./package.json` — **edit** `vitepress` and `vitepress-plugin-mermaid`

- `docs/.vitepress/config.ts` — **new** VitePress config (title, sidebar,

- `docs/.vitepress/sidebar.ts` — **new** sidebar generated from the Markdown

- `tests/main-street/docs-site-nav.test.ts` — **new** nav-coverage + drift-

- `tests/main-street/docs-path-drift.test.ts` — **edit** existing drift guard;

- `docs/README.md` — **edit** "Browsing these docs as a site" section (also

- `docs/index.md` — **new** docs-site landing page (also carries the AC10
  remote-browser note).
- `./README.md` — **edit** document the `docs*` npm scripts and the docs tree.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUNB54KU005084C** — Render the storyline graph (Mermaid→SVG) — completed (v0.1.19); this item is its deferred option (B).
- **MS-0MUYLLYX80090370** — Link & document the rendered storyline graph — completed; embedded the SVG in the canonical doc and documented regeneration.
- **MS-0MUZK0OWJ000PQ2D** — Restructure documentation (two-tree split) — established `docs/game/` + `docs/dev/`.
- **MS-0MUNC8AOL0092BE5** — Fix stale `example-games/main-street` paths — owner of the `docs-path-drift` guard.

## Assumptions

- The docs site is **local-only** (Q3=B): no CI build or Pages publishing is

- Navigation is the primary need (Q2=A); Mermaid fences are rendered in the

- **Toolchain adoption (LOW–MED).** VitePress is Vite-native (repo already

- **Q3 — Target audience / delivery?**

  - **Recommended: (A).**
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-17): (B)** — local dev tool only; **no CI

> All three answers recorded in comment MS-C0MVBVDIK0006YSM7.

- **Q4 — WSL / remote-browser access** (raised by the producer's audit
  rejection, 2026-10-23).
  - Observation: `npm run docs` serves at `http://localhost:5174/` but that URL

- **Build-time vs client-side Mermaid rendering — RESOLVED at implementation
  (2026-10-23).** The concern: the title says "render Mermaid docs at build
  time" while the Risks section permits client-side rendering for the
  local-only use case (Q3=B). Implementation chose **client-side rendering**

  cannot reach from the WSL dev server, even with `--host`; the printed network

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-19 — `/skill:plan` run: effort/risk pre-check returned **skip**

# Intake brief: Port the Vite watcher-ignore (`server.watch.ignored`) guard to sibling game repos' `vite.config.ts`

## Problem statement

The core scaffold template (CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA) emits `server.watch.ignored: [...DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS]` (covering `**/.worklog/**` and the dev-output trees), and `tce-main-street` and `tce-the-rising` already carry the block — but 8 sibling game repos' checked-in `vite.config.ts` still lack it: `AI_Hell`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`, `tce-blackjack`, `tce-coloretto`, `tce-feudalism`, `tce-golf`, `tce-lost-cities`, `tce-sushi-go`. When any of these repos accumulates `.worklog/worktrees/**` checkouts (AI_Hell already has 9 + a nested `ToneForge` checkout), the Vite/Vitest file watcher recursively walks them and exhausts the host `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` budget — `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers reached` — crashing the dev server and breaking test runs (the exact failure mode fixed in the parent item MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY).

## Users

- **Developers/agents working in any Tableau-Card-Engine game repo** (tce-\*) — must be able to run `npm run dev` and `npm test` from the main checkout once worktrees exist without tripping the host watcher limit.
  - *User story:* "As a developer in tce-blackjack, I want my dev server to ignore `.worklog/worktrees/**` so a recursive watch never exhausts inotify (ENOSPC)."
- **AI_Hell maintainers** (in scope — Q1 answered) — same failure mode is already active (9 worktree checkouts).
  - *User story:* "As an AI_Hell developer, I want the same watcher guard, so my `vite` dev server survives `.worklog/worktrees/**` growth."
- **Verification/audit tooling** — full-suite runs in sibling repos must not fail with ENOSPC.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Watcher guard present in every in-scope repo's checked-in config.** The 7 tce-\* repos each import `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` from `./core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin` and set `server.watch.ignored: [...DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS]` with the template's explanatory comment (wording as in CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA / `tce-the-rising`). AI_Hell (if in scope) sets `watch.ignored` from a locally defined constant covering `**/.worklog/**` (plus its dev-output trees). Verified per repo by grep of the checked-in file — no in-scope repo may lack the block.
2. **Per-repo regression guard test (mirrors the core/main-street ENOSPC guard).** Each tce-\* repo gains `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` (copy of main-street's, minus the in-process dev-server smoke; static assertions only): the real config imports the shared list, spreads it into `server.watch.ignored`, and the list covers `**/.worklog/**` plus `**/data/**`, `**/tmp/**`, `**/results/**`, `**/dist/**`. AI_Hell gains `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` asserting its local list covers `.worklog`. Each test is picked up by that repo's existing test projects and passes.
3. **Surgical port only.** No other template drift is synced: no `resolvePagesBase`/`base` backfill, no blind re-scaffold (sibling configs predate those template additions), no local-config changes (e.g. AI_Hell's `configCsvPlugin`, `open: true`, port settings) altered. Per-repo `git diff` touches only `vite.config.ts` plus the new guard test; pre-existing unrelated working-tree changes (`.gitignore`, untracked `AGENTS.md`/`.githooks/`/`.worklog/plugins/`) are never swept into a commit.
4. **Suites pass and changes land on each repo's `dev`.** Each in-scope repo's own test suite passes (agent-initiated runs go through the test skill, per repo), and each repo's change is committed on its `dev` branch and pushed to origin, with commits referencing `MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0` (precedent: cross-repo item MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV). The pre-existing 1-ahead-unpushed local commit on each sibling `dev` is accounted for at push time (see Constraints). tce-main-street itself has no source changes, so its suite is unaffected; full project suite (each modified repo) must pass with the changes.
5. **Documentation reflects the guard.** Config comment matches the core template wording; where a repo documents `npm run dev` (README/dev docs — currently none of the in-scope repos has a README), a matching note about the `.worklog/**` exclusion. CHANGELOG.md excluded — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **No core/TCE repository edits and no submodule moves.** The core scaffold template and its guard tests are already correct (CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA completed) and every sibling's pinned core commit (`09723c4b`) already exports `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` in `scripts/vite-transcript-plugin.ts` — verified.
- **Surgical only** — do **not** blind re-scaffold (`npm run scaffold` / `scaffold:games`): the current template additionally emits `resolvePagesBase`/production `base` behaviour that the sibling configs do not have; a re-scaffold would change more than the watch block. Port the `server.watch.ignored` block + import only.
- **Cross-repo working-tree isolation.** This item lives in tce-main-street's worklog but touches 8 sibling checkouts, all outside the tce-main-street worktree. Precedent MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV ("Cross-repo change ... Pushed to sibling dev") governs: edit each sibling checkout directly, commit per repo on its own `dev`, push per repo. tce-main-street's own worktree/main checkout stays untouched (no tce-main-street source change → no implement-worktree changes expected).
- **Respect pre-existing dirt.** Each sibling has unrelated uncommitted changes (`.gitignore` edits; untracked `AGENTS.md`, `.githooks/`, `.worklog/plugins/`). Never commit them; stage only `vite.config.ts` (+ new test).
- **Sibling `dev` is 1 commit ahead of origin** (an unpushed `.worklog/config.yaml` CTA commit, `WL-0MUWCGF670087GAS`). Pushing the port will carry that commit; if a non-fast-forward/push rejection occurs, resolve against that known baseline (do not rewrite others' pushed history).
- **Test-execution policy:** all agent-initiated test runs go through the test skill — run per repo (each sibling has its own CWD/worklog), never ad-hoc `npm test`/`vitest`.

## Existing state

- **Scaffolded siblings (7):** `tce-beleaguered-castle`, `tce-blackjack`, `tce-coloretto`, `tce-feudalism`, `tce-golf`, `tce-lost-cities`, `tce-sushi-go` — `vite.config.ts` is AUTO-GENERATED (scaffold `renderViteConfig`), identical to each other apart from the game name in the header comment, and each `server:` block has `port: 3000, open: false` only — no `watch.ignored`. Verified: `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` absent from all 7.
- **AI_Hell (1):** bespoke hand-written config (port 5173, `open: true`, `configCsvPlugin`, no `core` submodule) — no `server.watch` at all; it **cannot** import the core list. It already has 9 `.worklog/worktrees/**` checkouts (+ nested `ToneForge` checkout) — the ENOSPC failure mode is live there.
- **Exemplars:** `tce-main-street/vite.config.ts` and `tce-the-rising/vite.config.ts` already carry the block (main-street also has `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts`, the regression pattern to mirror; core has `game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` static guard).
- Siblings' core submodules are clean and pinned at `v0.1.17-201-g09723c4b`, which exports `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS`. Their `npm test` = `vitest run --project unit` with `include: ['tests/**/*.test.ts']`, and tsconfig includes `tests/**/*.ts` — new config tests are picked up automatically.

## Desired change

- **Per tce-\* repo:** in `vite.config.ts`, add `import { DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS } from './core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin';` and extend the `server:` block with `watch: { ignored: [...DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS] }` + the template's ENOSPC comment; add `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` (static assertions copied from main-street's guard).
- **AI_Hell (in scope — Q1 answered):** add a locally defined ignore constant (e.g. `vite/watchIgnore.ts`) mirroring the core list (or a scoped `.worklog`-focused list), wire `server: { watch: { ignored: [...] } }` into `vite.config.ts`, and add `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts`.
- Single source of truth stays in core; nothing in `core/` changes.

## Key Files:

- Each tce-\* repo: `vite.config.ts` — add `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` import + `server.watch.ignored` block
- Each tce-\* repo: `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` (new) — static config-wiring + pattern-coverage guard (mirror of `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` ENOSPC assertions and main-street's `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts`)
- AI_Hell: `vite.config.ts` — wire `watch.ignored`; `vite/watchIgnore.ts` (new) — local ignore constant; `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` (new) — guard test (AI_Hell test roots: `src`, `scripts`, `vite`)
- Reference only (no change): `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` (template already correct), `core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin.ts` (`DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` source), `tce-main-street/tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` (guard pattern to mirror)

## Related work

- MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY — Host inotify watcher exhaustion (ENOSPC) breaks main-checkout test runs (**parent; completed**; this item is its derived sibling port)
- CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA — core: `game-repo-scaffold` renderViteConfig omits `server.watch.ignored` (completed; template now emits it)
- CG-0MTJ7A4Z3000MFMV / CG-0MTJ560IZ005XAZC — core: vite-transcript-plugin ENOSPC hardening (completed)
- MS-0MVA50KJN009X30C — [test-failure] suite-exit failure (completed; same root cause family)
- MS-0MV5PNIPO00940KG — Main Street vite-node CLI test flake (completed; the local isolation that a blind re-scaffold would regress)
- MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV — Cross-repo change precedent: tracked in main-street worklog, "Pushed to sibling dev" AC (completed)
- MS-0MUQZH5PH001JXLV / MS-0MUQZH53F004ZKAN — Core scaffold Pages-base work (completed; the template drift deliberately **not** backfilled here)
- Note: sibling repos have their own worklog stores (some without a DB on disk); no sibling-side work items exist for this change — the main-street item is the tracking point.

## Assumptions & risks

- **Assumption (Q1 answered: include AI_Hell):** AI_Hell is in scope, handled via a locally defined ignore constant because it has no `core` submodule from which to import the shared list.
- **Risk (low):** chokidar ignore-glob semantics — `**/.worklog/**` covers `.worklog/worktrees/**`; validated by the core regression suite and main-street's in-process smoke. Sibling guards use the same static assertions.
- **Risk (medium):** list duplication in AI_Hell drifts from core over time — mitigation: comment in `vite/watchIgnore.ts` pointing at the core source (single source of truth), and the guard test pins `.worklog` coverage.
- **Risk (medium):** per-repo dev-server smoke tests ×8 would be slow/flaky under suite contention — mitigation: ship **static** config-wiring guards per repo (mirroring `game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`); the in-process `server.watcher.getWatched()` smoke stays where it already exists (main-street) — no new dev-server startups in siblings.
- **Risk (low):** push non-fast-forward on 7 sibling `dev` branches (each 1 local commit ahead of origin) — known baseline commit; rebase/stacking acceptable since those commits are local-only; surface anything unexpected rather than force-pushing.
- **Scope-creep risk:** syncing other stale template drift (`resolvePagesBase`/production `base`, `unit-cli` isolations, etc.) to siblings, or host inotify tuning, is tempting — recorded as related work (MS-0MUQZH5PH001JXLV etc.), NOT this item's scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: **Is AI_Hell in scope?** Its `vite.config.ts` is hand-written (not scaffold-generated), it has no `core` submodule, so the shared `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` list cannot be imported — the port there requires a locally duplicated ignore constant (drift risk), though its failure mode is already live (9 worktrees).
  - Options: (a) **Include AI_Hell** with a local ignore constant + guard test — rec, because the producer explicitly listed it and its ENOSPC risk is already active; (b) Exclude AI_Hell — port only the 7 scaffolded tce-\* repos and file a derived item in AI_Hell's own worklog (AH- prefix); (c) Include AI_Hell only if it adopts the core submodule (large, out of scope).
  - **Recommended:** (a) Include AI_Hell with a locally defined constant (comment referencing core as canonical source), pending producer confirmation.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-21):** Option **(a) — include AI_Hell** with a locally defined ignore constant + guard test, plus (as an additional ask) a follow-up work item in AI_Hell to bring its testing framework in line with the other repos. **Status: answered/closed.**
- Priority/type: kept `bug` / `low` as set — same root-cause family as parent MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY (reclassified chore→bug); `low` retained because for the 7 tce-\* repos with zero current worktrees the failure is latent, not actively blocking (AI_Hell's live state argues medium should AI_Hell be confirmed in scope).
- Research summary: verified all 8 repos lack the block (grep of checked-in configs); the 7 tce-\* configs are otherwise identical scaffold output (only the game name differs); each sibling's pinned core commit (`09723c4b`) already exports `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS`; `tce-the-rising` is the wired exemplar; main-street's `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` is the guard pattern to mirror; AI_Hell's test roots are `src`/`scripts`/`vite` with an exhaustive project-membership classifier (vite/ test auto-classified as unit). Cross-repo commit/push precedent: MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY** – Host inotify watcher exhaustion (ENOSPC) breaks main-checkout test runs (completed)
- **MS-0MUQZH45Y001OGBK** – Pages base-path build tests (completed)
- **MS-0MUQZH5PH001JXLV** – Core scaffold template Pages base (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: beleaguered, blackjack, blind, block, castle (+38 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: beleaguered, blackjack, block, castle, checked (+32 more)
- `core/CHANGELOG.md` — matched: 0mv5sehhg000zkua, beleaguered, blackjack, block, castle (+27 more)


## Plan

**Decomposition (8 parallel children — one per in-scope repo).** Each child is a
vertical slice through all layers for its repo: config wiring + regression guard
test + suite run through the test skill + commit/push on `dev` + commit recorded.
All children are independent (no dependency edges) — each repo's port is
self-contained, so the 7 scaffolded tce-\* ports can proceed in any order and
AI_Hell proceeds in parallel. Test-first ordering applies within each child
(guard test written before/with the config wiring).

|---|-------|------|----------|-------|

# Intake Brief — End of Turn summary dialog for competitive mode (MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI)

## Problem statement

The single-player End of Turn summary dialog (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41) gives the
player a deliberate review-and-advance moment after each turn. Competitive
(human-vs-AI) play has no equivalent: after the shared day's closing
presentation (`presentCompetitiveClosing`) the day auto-advances with only the
transient per-seat income text (`Player 1: +X coins | Player 2: +Y coins`, via
`perSeatClosingSummary`) and the incident reveal. There is no moment to compare
each seat's standing for the round just completed — businesses owned, income
and expenses per seat. This item extends the End of Turn summary dialog to
competitive mode: one panel per completed round (one shared day where every
seat finished and the closing ran), with **owner-keyed rows** (businesses
owned, income/expenses per seat).

## Users

- **Main Street competitive player (human seat)** — plays week-by-week against
  AI seats on the shared street; after each shared day's animations finish,
  wants a persistent panel showing every seat's round result and a deliberate
  "start the next day" action (parity with the single-player dialog).

**User stories:**

- As a competitive player, when the shared day's closing animations finish, I
  see one panel summarising the round with a row per seat (businesses owned,
  income, expenses, net change, closing coins/reputation/score) so I can
  compare standings and learn from the round.
- As a competitive player, I click **[ Next Turn ]** to start the next shared
  day — the day does not advance until I do.
- As a competitive player, I see the same (disabled) **[ Bank Loan ]**
  affordance as the single-player dialog, so the loans option is planned and
  consistent across modes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In competitive play (N ≥ 2), after the shared closing presentation completes, a Turn Summary dialog appears with one panel per completed round — one owner-keyed row per non-eliminated seat showing businesses owned, income (with the per-phase breakdown), ongoing expenses per category (staff / community / business), net coin change, and closing coins / reputation / score; the next shared day does **not** start until the player clicks **[ Next Turn ]**, and reduced-motion, replay and headless/AI-driven paths skip the dialog and keep the existing auto-advance pacing.
2. The dialog content is **engine-computed and owner-keyed**: the competitive close surfaces per-seat ongoing costs, businesses owned and net change on `TurnResult` (extending the parent item's owner-keyed ledger design), so every value shown is testable without a browser and consistent with the single-player ledger; additions are optional and backwards-compatible — `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`, `presentCompetitiveClosing` and the headless/Monte-Carlo paths are unaffected when the field is absent.
3. The dialog reuses the single-player Turn Summary presentation: the Phaser-free model renders owner-keyed rows (reusing the competitive scoreboard's `You`/`AI n` labels and `resolveSeatColour` seat colours); **[ Next Turn ]** (primary) and **[ Bank Loan ]** (**disabled** with an explanatory hint, behind the same single wiring seam that MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG replaces — never enabled by this item) buttons; overlay conventions: `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton`, elements in `s.hudContainer`, depths 199/200/201, pushed into `s.overlayObjects`, `safePlaySound` for the button SFX.
4. Single-player behaviour is unchanged; the competitive gate slots only in the scene presentation tail — between `presentCompetitiveClosing` completing and `startTurnPhase` in `presentCompetitiveDayTail` — and never in the engine/headless close path; checkpoint save ordering (`presentCompetitiveDayTail` saves before the closing) is unchanged, and the dialog adds no save and mutates no state.
5. At least one automated test per surfaced value (Phaser-free model tests for owner-keyed rows, engine per-seat ledger tests, and a competitive-mode browser dialog test); **all related documentation is updated** (docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md competitive closing and end-of-turn summary sections, plus any README/dev references); **the full project test suite passes** with the changes.

## Constraints

- **Blocked-by MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** (outbound dependency): the parent item is
  still `open` (stage `intake_complete`) — its `TurnResult` owner-keyed ledger
  does **not exist in the code yet**. This item builds on and consumes that
  ledger; implementers must land/coordinate with the parent first. Per-seat
  expense capture does not exist anywhere today — `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`
  returns `void` and only logs — so the per-seat ledger extension is real
  engine work on top of the parent's ledger shape (kept optional and
  backwards-compatible throughout).
- Presentation-only contract: the dialog reads committed state / `result` and
  never mutates engine state or consumes RNG. In competitive, deltas are
  already applied to each `PlayerRecord` before the closing is presented, so
  the panel shows post-round values; the checkpoint save stays in
  `presentCompetitiveDayTail` (existing ordering).
- Overlay conventions (AGENTS.md UI best practices) exactly as the parent
  item constrains: `createOverlayBackground` + `createOverlayButton` from
  `@ui`; elements parented into `s.hudContainer`; depths 199 / 200 / 201;
  everything pushed into `s.overlayObjects` for dismissal; instant appearance
  (reduced-motion safe); button SFX via `safePlaySound`.
- Headless determinism and bounded pacing must not regress: Monte-Carlo /
  AI headless days (`MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`, `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`)
  never invoke the scene presentation and must never show/block on the dialog;
  the competitive closing bound (`COMPETITIVE_CLOSING_MAX_TOTAL_MS`) stays.
- **Assumption (Q-scope, from repo evidence):** a "round" equals **one
  completed shared day** — all non-eliminated seats finished and the shared
  closing ran. The engine has no separate "round" concept beyond the shared
  day (`round-robin` seat iteration only), so "one panel per completed round"
  = one dialog per shared day.
- **Assumption (blocking safety):** competitive is human-vs-AI on one device
  (no networked multiplayer), so a blocking dialog gated on the single human
  seat cannot stall other humans. Interactive Q1 = A.
- The parent item's banking-hint ordering assumption is single-player-only and
  does not apply to the competitive panel (no banking-hint step exists in the
  competitive closing).
- `TurnResult` / `OwnerIncomeResult` additions must not break competitive
  callers (`MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`, `presentCompetitiveClosing`,
  `perSeatClosingSummary`, scoreboard/HUD consumers) — keep ledger fields
  optional/absent-undefined-safe and guard with tests.

## Existing state

- `endCompetitiveTurnDay` (`src/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`):
  ends the human's MarketPhase, drives AI seats to the shared closing, runs
  `runCompetitiveClosing`, then `presentCompetitiveDayTail` →
  station checkpoint save → `presentCompetitiveClosing(closing, () =>
  startTurnPhase())`. The new gate slots at the end of the closing
  presentation, before `startTurnPhase` (presentation path only).
- `TurnResult.playerIncome?: OwnerIncomeResult[]` **already exists**
  (`src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts`): owner-keyed income, non-eliminated seats,
  in seat order, populated by `applyCompetitiveIncome`
  (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`, through `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases`
  in `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`). Each entry carries
  `income.phaseBreakdown.perSlotBreakdown` (base / synergy / reputation /
  events / upcoming slots per owner).
- Per-seat ongoing costs are computed in `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`
  (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`) — staff salaries per owner, community +
  business running costs per slot owner via `ownerTaggedGrid` — but are
  **not surfaced** on any result (void, log-only). Businesses owned per seat
  are derivable from `ownerTaggedGrid` / `getSlotOwnerId`
  (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`).
- Per-seat row conventions exist in `buildCompetitiveScoreboard`
  (`src/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard.ts`): `You` / `AI n` labels,
  `resolveSeatColour` seat colours, coin/rep/score columns — reused by the
  Game Over overlay model `MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts`.
- Overlay precedent and single-player dialog model come from
  MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41 (its `MainStreetTurnSummary` model +
  `showTurnSummaryDialog`); docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md documents the
  competitive closing presentation (section "Competitive phase-major closing
  presentation …"), including the current auto-advance behaviour that this
  item changes.

## Desired change

1. Engine: capture and surface the per-seat round ledger on `TurnResult` —
   per-owner ongoing expenses (staff / community / business), businesses
   owned, net coin change — extending the `OwnerIncomeResult` shape (or the
   parent's owner-keyed ledger) inside `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` /
   `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`; keep everything optional so
   single-player, N=1 and headless calls are untouched.
2. Model: extend the single-player Phaser-free `MainStreetTurnSummary` to
   render **owner-keyed competitive rows** (seat label + colour from the
   competitive scoreboard conventions) for the round just closed.
3. UI: extend the single-player `showTurnSummaryDialog(...)` (or a thin
   competitive sibling sharing the same panel) with **[ Next Turn ]**
   (primary) and a **disabled [ Bank Loan ]** button behind the shared wiring
   seam; gate `presentCompetitiveDayTail` so the deferred
   (animations-enabled) path presents the dialog when the closing completes
   and only calls `startTurnPhase` after **[ Next Turn ]** — reduced-motion /
   replay / headless keep today's auto-advance.
4. Tests and docs: Phaser-free model tests, engine per-seat ledger tests, a
   competitive browser dialog test; update docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md
   (competitive closing + end-of-turn summary sections).

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` — gate `presentCompetitiveDayTail` on the dialog (between closing-complete and `startTurnPhase`); presentation path only
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` / `finishCompetitiveClosingTail`: surface the per-seat round ledger on `TurnResult`
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`: return/capture the per-owner expense breakdown (staff / community / business)
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` — extend `TurnResult` (and/or `OwnerIncomeResult`) with the optional owner-keyed round ledger (expenses, businesses owned, net change)
- `src/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` / `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — `OwnerIncomeResult` shape extension
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — extend the Phaser-free summary model to render owner-keyed competitive rows (reusing scoreboard label/colour conventions)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` + `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — dialog presentation + delegation (shared with the single-player panel); `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton` per overlay conventions
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard.ts` — reuse `You` / `AI n` labels, `resolveSeatColour` colours for rows
- Docs: `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (competitive closing + end-of-turn summary sections)
- Tests: `tests/main-street/turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts` (pure model), `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-ledger.test.ts` (engine), `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` (competitive overlay)

## Related work

### Automated related-work report (`find_related.py`)

- **MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** – End of Turn summary dialog (single-player seed)
  (open)
- **MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG** – Bank Loans (open)
- **MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ** – Refactor end-of-turn presentation: remove
  single-player/competitive duplication and add per-seat income feedback
  (completed)
- Repository matches: `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `core/AGENTS.md`,
  `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (keyword overlap: competitive,
  ledger, end-of-turn, dialog, seat, round, businesses).
- Duplicate check: `wl search "turn summary competitive"` returned only the
  parent, the deferred Bank Loans seam and End of game stats — **no
  overlapping completed item**; no duplicate/partial-overlap rewrite needed.

### Hand-curated context

- `MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41` — **parent / blocked-by**: single-player End of Turn
  summary dialog + `TurnResult` owner-keyed ledger; this item's panel consumes
  that ledger and the parent's overlay/model. Not yet implemented (open,
  intake_complete) — ordering constraint.
- `MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG` — **Bank Loans**: the seam this item's disabled Bank
  Loan button exposes; enablement blocked by that item (shared with
  single-player panel).
- `MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV` — **End of game stats** (open, low): turn-by-turn
  history + graphs on Game Over; consumes the same per-turn ledger data
  (synergy, not duplication — distinct screen).
- `MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ` (completed) — end-of-turn presentation refactor:
  source of today's `closingSummary` / shared closing primitive.
- `MS-0MUXAQQON006XA6I` + `MS-0MUYFXA36009EMH0` (completed) — competitive
  per-seat income choreography and per-seat animated closing: the cadence this
  panel extends; `TurnResult.playerIncome` originates here.
- `MS-0MUWDL0V40041USM` (completed) — game-over overlay epic: the
  Phaser-free-model + overlay-convention precedent (`MainStreetGameOverSummary`
  reusing `buildCompetitiveScoreboard`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (round = day):** "one panel per completed round" maps to one
  panel per completed shared day (every seat finished + closing ran); the
  engine has no separate round concept. Recorded from repo evidence; if a
  day-vs-round distinction exists conceptually (e.g. a preset defining round
  length), the panel cadence would need revisiting — flagged for implementer
  verification.
- **Assumption (single human seat):** competitive is human-vs-AI on one
  device, so a blocking dialog on the human's **[ Next Turn ]** cannot stall
  other humans; multifloored safety holds for the current product shape.
  (If networked multiplayer ever lands, blocking semantics need a per-seat
  pause protocol.)
- **Risk (parent not landed):** the owner-keyed ledger this item consumes does
  not exist yet; if the parent lands without the per-seat expense capture
  (today `void`/log-only), this item must extend it — keep additions optional
  and guarded so `presentCompetitiveClosing` and headless/Monte-Carlo flows are
  byte-stable when absent.
- **Risk (blocking regresses headless pacing):** the gate must live in the
  scene presentation tail only (`presentCompetitiveDayTail`), never in engine
  close functions; Monte-Carlo / AI headless days never touch the scene and
  must continue to auto-advance under `COMPETITIVE_CLOSING_MAX_TOTAL_MS`.
- **Risk (eliminated seats):** the closing already omits eliminated seats from
  `playerIncome`; the panel must render exactly the seats the closing surfaced
  (no ghost rows for bankrupt/eliminated seats) and say so in its test.
- **Risk (loans are per-owner):** the shared disabled Bank Loan seam is a
  single hook today; when MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG lands, competitive loans are
  likely per-seat — keep the seam shaped so it can become
  `onBankLoanAction(seatId)` without re-plumbing the panel.
- **Scope-creep risk:** per-round history across days (post-game stats,
  MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV), networked multiplayer, live loans
  (MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG) and any round-summary log/graph features are outside
  this item; tracked as linked items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Blocking behaviour — in single-player the dialog blocks the next-day
  advance until [ Next Turn ] is clicked; in competitive the day currently
  auto-advances after the closing presentation. Options: A) Block like
  single-player — next day starts only after [ Next Turn ]. B) Non-blocking —
  panel appears but the day advances behind it / auto-dismisses."
  — Answer (operator): "A". Source: interactive reply, intake session
  MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI, 2026-10-25. (Recommended option was A — consistency
  with the single-player dialog; accepted as chosen.)
- Q2: "Per-seat data source — per-seat expenses aren't captured anywhere
  today (TurnResult.playerIncome covers income only). Options: A) Extend the
  engine with an owner-keyed per-seat ledger on TurnResult (per-seat ongoing
  costs, businesses owned, net change — engine-computed, testable headless),
  mirroring the parent's ledger. B) Derive presentation-only at panel time
  from committed state."
  — Answer (operator): "A". Source: interactive reply, intake session
  MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI, 2026-10-25. (Recommended option was A — matches the
  parent item's owner-keyed ledger design intent; accepted as chosen.)
- Q3: "Bank Loan button parity — the single-player dialog renders a disabled
  [ Bank Loan ] button with a wiring seam for MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG. Options:
  A) Same disabled Bank Loan button in the competitive panel (parity).
  B) Omit it — strictly the seed's content."
  — Answer (operator): "A". Source: interactive reply, intake session
  MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI, 2026-10-25. (Recommended option was A — one shared
  loans seam avoids divergent affordances; accepted as chosen.)

# Intake brief: Remove broken `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` npm scripts from generated game repos

**Type:** chore · **Priority:** low · **Cross-repo:** yes (Tableau-Card-Engine core via the `./core` submodule) · **Discovered-from:** MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL

## Problem statement

Every generated game repo (`tce-main-street`, `tce-golf`, `tce-blackjack`, …) declares two npm scripts — `scaffold:game` and `scaffold:games` — that point at `tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, a file that does **not** exist in a game repo (Option C: game repos have no root `scripts/` tree; the scaffold lives in the core at `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`). Invoking either script fails with a module-not-found error. The working game-repo entry point, `npm run scaffold`, passes `--core-root ./core` and exists in every generated repo.

Root cause (resolved): `renderPackageJson` in `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` inherits the **entire** core `scripts` map from the core manifest (line ~280: `...Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(manifest.scripts ?? {}))`). `core/package.json` legitimately declares `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` for core-repo use, so both leak unmodified into every generated game repo. The description's open "which is true" question is answered: the template **does** emit them, but only by inheritance — the fix is a template-side filter, not merely deleting two lines from each repo.

## Users

- **Game-repo maintainers (agents and humans)** — run npm scripts inside a game repo without tripping over dead entries.
  - *User story:* "As a maintainer of tce-main-street, I want `npm run scaffold:game` to either work or not be declared, so a script listed in my repo never fails with module-not-found."
- **Core scaffold owners (Tableau-Card-Engine)** — keep the template emitting only what a game repo can actually run.
  - *User story:* "As a core template owner, I want the scaffold to filter core-only scripts (including any future ones) out of generated repos, so a re-scaffold never reintroduces broken entries."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **This repo's `package.json` no longer declares `scaffold:game` or `scaffold:games`.** `npm run scaffold` remains and resolves to `tsx ./core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --game main-street ...`. Guarded by a regression test (new `tests/tooling/scaffold-scripts.test.ts`) asserting the two broken keys are absent and every `scaffold*` script's target file exists.
2. **The scaffold template stops emitting them.** `renderPackageJson` in `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` filters the core-only `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` entries out of the inherited scripts map. Add a unit test in `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` whose manifest declares both keys and asserts the rendered `package.json` omits them, so a re-scaffold cannot reintroduce them (AC2 of the original item).
3. **The core change is delivered.** `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` + its test land in Tableau-Card-Engine (CG work item, per the MS↔CG pairing precedent of MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED↔CG-0MVD0IZDR008921Q); this repo records the engine commit via its `./core` submodule pointer bump (`npm run engine:sync`), and `npm run scaffold` on a fixture checkout regenerates a `package.json` without the two keys.
4. **Documentation.** `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` documents `npm run scaffold` as the game-repo scaffold entry point and states that `scaffold:game(s)` are core-checkout-only commands; no game-repo-context doc references `scaffold:game(s)`. Core docs that use them (DEVELOPER.md, dev/creating-a-new-game.md, dev/multi-repo-architecture.md) are core-checkout context and remain accurate; a one-line "run from the core checkout" clarification is made where ambiguity exists.
5. **Validation.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes (changed-scope test gate plus the added regression tests; core-side suite green in the engine repo). The new `tests/tooling/` file is collected by the existing `unit` project (`tests/**/*.test.ts`, `vite.config.ts:222`) — no project-config change needed.

> **Traceability to the original ACs:** brief AC1 ← original AC1; brief AC2 + AC3 ← original AC2 ("resolve which is true first" resolved: the template emits them by inheritance, so a template filter is required); brief AC4 ← original AC3; brief AC5 ← original AC4.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo delivery** — the template fix lives in the Tableau-Card-Engine repo (`core/` submodule); this item cannot satisfy AC2 in-repo. Push policy applies to both repos: `dev` only.
- **No `npm run scaffold` against the live checkout** — re-scaffolding this repo today **drops 10 locally-added scripts** (`docs`, `docs:build`, `docs:preview`, `pretest`, `test:browser`, `generate:pack-assets`, `validate:storylines`, `storylines:graph:svg`, `docs:diagrams`, `balance:synergy-diversity-report`) because the template does not preserve repo-local extras. AC1 must be done with a hand edit; fixture-based re-scaffold verification lives in tests.
- **No CI beyond npm builds** — the npm build/test scripts are the verification vehicle.
- Implementation follows the mandatory worktree + build→test→commit order of the implement skill; work-item tracking via wl only.

## Existing state

- Issue type stays `chore`: the change removes dead config keys and adjusts the scaffold's config generation; it changes no runtime app behaviour (matches the `discovered-from` item's classification).

- `package.json` (this repo, lines 34–35): `"scaffold:game": "tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts"`, `"scaffold:games": "tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --all --core-root . --repos-dir .."`. Root `scripts/` contains only `run-tests.ts` and `soak-browser-waits.sh` — the target does not exist.
- `package.json` line 50: `"scaffold": "tsx ./core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --game main-street --game-repo-root . --core-root ./core"` — the working entry point (exists in all sibling repos too).

# Verification: remote pack discovery, integrity & degradation

## Goal

Prove — with automated tests — that a remote pack catalogue is discovered,
cryptographically verified, and safely degraded when anything goes wrong, so
the parent's discovery, degradation, rejection and integrity criteria are
met by evidence rather than assertion.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent ACs 1, 3, 4 and 6).

## Scope

Verification-only: this item adds or hardens tests and fixtures; it does not
add production behaviour. Where a test exposes a real gap in the remote
source, record the gap and raise a comment on the sibling feature item rather
than implementing the fix here.

Coverage to establish:

1. **Discovery.** A pack catalogue served from a configured host appears in
   the discovery result alongside bundled packs, with its manifest, cards CSV
   and pack id intact.
2. **Signature gate.** A valid signature loads; missing, invalid, wrong-key,
   and malformed-envelope manifests each reject the source **whole** (every
   path from that source resolves `null`) with exactly one warning.
3. **Degradation.** Unreachable host, connection rejection, HTTP error,
   slow/hung host (bounded timeout), and malformed manifest JSON each leave
   boot on bundled content, never throw, and never leave the Card Packs
   listing empty when a bundled pack exists.
4. **Rejection of bad data.** A pack whose CSV header is wrong, or whose card
   ids duplicate an already-accepted pack, is rejected by the existing core
   merge without affecting packs from other sources.

Tests must use an injected fake `fetch`/transport and injected timers so the
suite never performs real network I/O and never waits a real 3 seconds.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Remote discovery is covered: a signed remote pack served by a fake
      transport appears in `loadMainStreetCardPacks`' result with its cards
      merged into the pool.
- [ ] Every signature failure mode is covered: missing signature, invalid
      signature, signature from a non-pinned key, and malformed envelope each
      reject the whole source and emit exactly one warning.
- [ ] Every degradation mode is covered: unreachable host, rejected fetch,
      non-2xx response, timeout abort, and unparseable manifest each boot on
      bundled content with no throw.
- [ ] A test asserts the timeout is bounded at the configured value using fake
      timers — no test waits on a real clock.
- [ ] A test asserts the Card Packs listing input is non-empty when a bundled
      pack exists and the remote source fails.
- [ ] Bad pack data (wrong header, duplicate card ids) is covered as rejected
      whole without affecting sibling sources.
- [ ] No test performs real network I/O; every fetch goes through an injected
      transport.

# Verification: remote pack precedence, gating & asset parity

## Goal

Prove that remote packs are indistinguishable from bundled packs at the
registry, gating and asset layers, and that precedence is deterministic, so the
parent's parity, precedence and asset-resolution criteria are evidenced by
automated tests.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent ACs 2, 5 and 7).

## Scope

Verification-only: this item adds tests and fixtures; it does not add
production behaviour. Gaps found are reported on the sibling feature items.

Coverage to establish:

1. **Precedence — bundled wins.** A pack id present in both the bundled and a
   remote source is served from the bundled source, byte-for-byte.
2. **Precedence — remote first-wins.** Two remote sources carrying the same
   pack id resolve to the first-registered source's content.
3. **Registry composition.** The composed registry order is bundled first,
   then remote sources in configured URL order; registration is idempotent by
   id and never reorders existing sources.
4. **Gating parity.** An entitled remote pack is loaded; an unentitled remote
   pack is `locked` and contributes no rows; the scoped simulated purchase
   promotes the declared remote pack and re-discovers it — the same flow as
   the bundled residential pack.
5. **Persistence parity.** A save created with a remote pack active restores
   the same active pack set and merged checksum after a load round-trip.
6. **Asset parity.** A remote pack's `assetUrls` entries resolve to absolute
   URLs on the configured remote base, are gated on manifest verification, and
   reject traversal/undeclared asset paths.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test asserts bundled content wins over a remote source carrying the
      same pack id (byte-for-byte comparison).
- [ ] A test asserts first-wins between two remote sources in registration
      order.
- [ ] A test asserts the composed registry order is bundled → remote(s) in
      configured order, and that re-adding a source is a no-op.
- [ ] A test asserts an unentitled remote pack is reported `locked` and
      contributes no merged rows.
- [ ] A test asserts the scoped simulated purchase unlocks the declared remote
      pack and the post-purchase discovery loads it.
- [ ] A save/load round-trip test asserts the active remote pack set and merged
      checksum are preserved.
- [ ] A test asserts remote `assetUrls` resolve to the configured remote base,
      that a rejected source resolves no assets, and that undeclared or
      traversal asset paths resolve `null`.
- [ ] Changed-scope tests pass through the test skill.

- `tests/main-street/fixtures/remotePackFixtures.ts`

# Turn summary dialog suppressed by reduced motion setting

Discovered from: MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41 (End of Turn summary) / MS-0MVP46AMO002SZUT (dialog overlay).

## Problem

The Turn Summary dialog (MS-0MVP46AMO002SZUT) never appears for a player with the
reduced-motion setting enabled, even though the dialog itself is instant-appearance
(no fade, no tween) and therefore reduced-motion safe. The closing silently
auto-advances instead of pausing on the summary.

## Root Cause — two separate reduced-motion gates

1. **Display gate.** `shouldGateTurnSummary` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`, ~line 544)
   returns `false` when `settingsPanel.reducedMotion === true`, so the dialog is never presented:

   ```ts
   if (s.replayMode === true) return false;
   if (s.settingsPanel?.reducedMotion === true) return false;   // <-- culprit
   ```

2. **Path gate (deeper).** Even if gate 1 is removed the dialog still cannot appear, because
   reduced motion never takes the deferred-closing path that the dialog gates. In `endTurn`
   (`MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`, ~line 229):

   ```ts
   const deferred = !inTutorialBefore && !reducedMotion && !s.replayMode;
   ...
   result = processEndOfTurn(s.state, deferred ? { deferResourceApplication: true } : undefined);
   ```

   The engine only sets `requiresDeferredClosing: true` when `deferResourceApplication` is
   passed (`MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`, ~line 776). `shouldGateTurnSummary`'s first
   guard is `if (result.requiresDeferredClosing !== true) return false;`, so a reduced-motion
   closing has no deferred result and the gate is a no-op — the immediate path advances the
   day with no dialog. Removing only the display gate would therefore change nothing.

## Fix

Both need to change so that reduced motion is honoured by *animations* but not by the
*dialog*:

1. Remove the `reducedMotion === true` early return from `shouldGateTurnSummary`
   (keep replay / tutorial / competitive guards).
2. Let reduced motion take the deferred-closing path in `endTurn`, so
   `requiresDeferredClosing` is set and the gate has something to gate (keep tutorial and
   replay on their existing immediate paths). The reduced-motion animator already finalizes
   its income/incident presentation without tweens, so the deferred closing completes
   promptly; `deferUntilIncomeCollected` stays bounded so the closing can never hang.

Design note: with reduced motion the phased income show still schedules its
`INCOME_PHASE_GAP_MS` (2.2 s) phase slots before the collect step runs, so the summary may
appear up to ~2.2 s × number of non-empty phases later. Confirm that pacing is acceptable,
or skip the empty-phase time in reduced motion, so the dialog does not feel like a hang.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A reduced-motion single-player `endTurn` produces a result with
   `requiresDeferredClosing === true` and `shouldGateTurnSummary` returns `true`.
2. The Turn Summary dialog is presented for reduced-motion players, and `[ Next Turn ]`
   resumes the deferred closing exactly once (day advances, HUD shows post-delta values).
3. Existing guards still suppress the dialog for replay, tutorial and competitive closings.
4. The dialog stays instant-appearance (no fade/tween) and plays SFX via `safePlaySound`
   (mute respected); no new animation is introduced for reduced motion.
5. Unit tests cover the guard matrix (reduced motion on/off × replay × tutorial ×
   competitive) and the `endTurn` deferred-path selection under reduced motion; a browser
   test asserts the dialog appears after a reduced-motion end-of-turn.
6. Changed-scope test gate passes; the dev-push gate (full suite) passes before merge.
